edges.mechanism: Zinc chelates fluoroquinolones in the gut and lowers antibiotic absorption. A zinc-containing multivitamin lowered ciprofloxacin AUC from 14.5 to 11.3 ug.h/mL.
edges.evidence: Crossover PK study (n=12) plus FDA ciprofloxacin label (take 2 h before or 6 h after zinc products).

edges.mechanism: Zinc chelates tetracycline. 45 mg zinc as sulfate cut tetracycline absorption by about 30%; doxycycline was not significantly affected.
edges.evidence: Crossover PK study (n=7); doses should be separated.

edges.mechanism: Metal binding in the gut inactivates penicillamine. The label requires at least 1 h separation from zinc- or iron-containing products and says mineral supplements may block its response. In Wilson disease the Galzin label found no pharmacodynamic interaction under supervised use.
edges.evidence: FDA labels; guideline context for Wilson disease.

edges.mechanism: Thiazides raise urinary zinc excretion (total zinc excretion +60%), which may deplete zinc stores over time.
edges.evidence: Small randomized/observational studies plus SR of zinc and antihypertensives.

edges.mechanism: Captopril (more than enalapril) raises urinary zinc and lowers cell zinc. Losartan and valsartan have been linked to zinc loss.
edges.evidence: Small clinical studies and SR; low certainty.

edges.mechanism: Raised gastric pH reduces absorption of zinc supplements. On long-term PPIs plasma zinc rose 37% versus 126% in controls; short-term omeprazole did not affect zinc absorption from food.
edges.evidence: Small human absorption studies; conflicting.

edges.mechanism: Zinc lowers fasting glucose (about -14 mg/dL) and HbA1c (about -0.55%), so it may add to glucose-lowering drugs.
edges.evidence: MAs of RCTs; low certainty; no direct interaction studies.

edges.mechanism: Non-heme iron competes with zinc for absorption (Fe:Zn 2:1 or more inhibits), but heme iron at a 3:1 ratio did not inhibit zinc absorption. Zinc inhibits non-heme iron absorption at Zn:Fe molar ratios of 5:1 or more. In children, adding iron blunted zinc's benefits.
edges.evidence: Human absorption studies and Cochrane subgroup finding; heme-specific interaction appears small.

edges.mechanism: Calcium reduces zinc absorption: 600 mg CaCO3 with a meal halved zinc absorption, and an extra 468 mg/d calcium cut net zinc absorption by about 2 mg/d.
edges.evidence: Human balance and absorption studies (off-list supplement).

edges.mechanism: High-dose zinc (142 mg/d) lowers magnesium absorption and balance. Refractory hypomagnesaemia has been reported with postoperative zinc.
edges.evidence: Metabolic balance study plus case report.

edges.mechanism: Quercetin acts as a zinc ionophore, raising intracellular labile zinc in cells and liposomes. Clinical relevance is unknown.
edges.evidence: In vitro only; no human outcome data.

edges.mechanism: Zinc induces enterocyte metallothionein, which traps copper. Chronic excess causes copper deficiency with anaemia, neutropenia and myeloneuropathy. Copper status should be checked or copper added (AREDS added 2 mg) during long-term high-dose zinc (off-list supplement).
edges.evidence: SR of 37 cases, case reports, FDA Galzin label warning, AREDS design.

edges.mechanism: These are co-components of the AREDS2 formula for intermediate AMD. Lutein/zeaxanthin replacing beta-carotene gave HR 0.85 for late AMD versus beta-carotene, without the lung-cancer signal.
edges.evidence: AREDS2 RCT and 10-year follow-up; Cochrane review.

edges.mechanism: In the AREDS antioxidant-plus-zinc arm, advanced AMD OR was 0.72 versus 0.75 for zinc alone. Adding high-dose vitamin C to zinc gave no benefit in COVID-19 outpatients.
edges.evidence: AREDS RCT; COVID A to Z RCT.

edges.mechanism: Vitamin E is a component of the AREDS formula; antioxidants plus zinc reduced progression to advanced AMD.
edges.evidence: AREDS RCT and Cochrane review; moderate certainty.

edges.mechanism: Phytate binds zinc and is thought to limit absorption from plant-based diets. In children, low-phytate maize did not raise zinc absorption and phytate had no detectable effect.
edges.evidence: Stable-isotope studies in children; adult effect not studied here.

edges.mechanism: Zinc salts are a guideline-endorsed maintenance therapy. Use requires specialist monitoring of urinary copper and ALT, and chelators are preferred in significant liver disease.
edges.evidence: EASL-ERN guideline 2025, retrospective cohort, FDA label.

edges.mechanism: Applying zinc to the olfactory epithelium causes hyposmia or anosmia, which can be permanent; causation is supported by Bradford Hill criteria.
edges.evidence: Case series (17 and 25 patients) and causality analysis.

edges.mechanism: No reduction in diarrhoea duration, and more vomiting (RR 1.54).
edges.evidence: Cochrane review; moderate certainty.

edges.mechanism: Zinc activates the metalloenzyme ALP. 50 mg/d raised total and bone ALP, and zinc acetate therapy can raise ALP, amylase and lipase.
edges.evidence: Small RCTs and FDA label; a true physiological change, not an assay artefact.

edges.mechanism: Zinc lowers serum copper and ceruloplasmin activity; low values during zinc use suggest zinc-induced copper deficiency.
edges.evidence: Crossover trial (150 mg/d), case reports, SR.

edges.mechanism: In healthy people, zinc lowered HDL by 0.10 mmol/L (about 7%); in T2D, HDL rose.
edges.evidence: MA of 33 interventions; T2D MA.
